hook.line: A compliment with a built-in expectation: "for a beginner, that's good". Spanish does it with *para*, but not the *para* you know from "in order to".
hook.es: No está mal para ser la primera vez.
hook.en: Not bad for a first time.

examples.es: No está mal para ser la primera vez.
examples.en: Not bad for a first time.

examples.es: Para ser tan joven, sabe mucho.
examples.en: For someone so young, she knows a lot.

examples.es: Habla muy bien para llevar solo un año aquí.
examples.en: He speaks very well considering he's only been here a year.

examples.es: Para ser apenas las ocho, ya hay mucho tráfico.
examples.en: For only eight o'clock, there's already a lot of traffic.

examples.es: Para ser un martes, hay mucha gente en el café.
examples.en: For a Tuesday, there are a lot of people in the café.

examples.es: La torta quedó muy buena para ser la primera vez.
examples.en: The cake came out very good for a first time.

rule:
Here *para* doesn't mean purpose. It means "considering" or "for": you measure something against what you would normally expect. *Para ser tan joven, sabe mucho.*

The pattern is *para ser* plus a noun or description, or *para llevar* plus a length of time: *habla bien para llevar un año aquí*. It can come first or last in the sentence.

Don't swap in *por*. *Por ser tan joven* gives a cause ("because he's so young"). *Para ser tan joven* gives a surprise ("for someone so young").
smallPrint: Teachers call this *para* of comparison or concession. The set phrase *para ser sincero* ("to be honest") is different.

readAndPick.es: Para ser tan joven, sabe mucho.
options: For someone so young, she knows a lot.
Because she is so young, she knows a lot.
She is young in order to know a lot.

readAndPick.es: Por ser tan joven, no la contrataron.
options: For someone so young, they didn't hire her.
Because she is so young, they didn't hire her.
They didn't hire her to be young.

readAndPick.es: No está mal para ser la primera vez.
options: Not bad for a first time.
It's bad because it's the first time.
It isn't the first time.
He's quite good for a doctor.
He studies in order to be a doctor.
He studies because he is a doctor.

readAndPick.es: Habla muy bien para llevar solo un año aquí.
options: He speaks well in order to stay a year.
He speaks very well, considering he's only been here a year.
He has been here a year because he speaks well.

readAndPick.es: Para ser un martes, hay mucha gente.
options: For a Tuesday, there are a lot of people.
It is Tuesday in order to have people.
There are people because it's Tuesday.

readAndPick.es: Por ser un martes, hay poca gente.
options: For a Tuesday, there are few people.
Because it's a Tuesday, there are few people.
There are few people to be a Tuesday.

readAndPick.es: La torta quedó muy buena para ser la primera vez.
options: The cake was very good because it was the first time.
The cake was very good for a first time.
The cake was made for the first time.
I work to be better.
I'm good for someone who works.
I work because I'm better.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right word and type the whole sentence: *___ ser tan joven, sabe mucho.* (*Para* or *Por*, a surprise)
yourTurn.answer: Para ser tan joven, sabe mucho.
yourTurn.why: A surprise measured against what you would expect takes *para*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right word and type the whole sentence: *___ ser tan joven, no la contrataron.* (*Para* or *Por*, a cause)
yourTurn.answer: Por ser tan joven, no la contrataron.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Not bad for a first time.
yourTurn.answer: No está mal para ser la primera vez.
yourTurn.why: *No está mal* plus *para ser* and the thing you are comparing with.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: For a Tuesday, there are a lot of people in the café.
yourTurn.answer: Para ser un martes, hay mucha gente en el café.
accept: Hay mucha gente en el café para ser un martes.
yourTurn.why: *Para ser* plus the noun, and it can sit at either end.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: He speaks very well considering he's only been here a year.
yourTurn.answer: Habla muy bien para llevar solo un año aquí.
accept: Para llevar solo un año aquí, habla muy bien.
yourTurn.why: With a length of time, use *para llevar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: For only eight o'clock, there's already a lot of traffic.
yourTurn.answer: Para ser apenas las ocho, ya hay mucho tráfico.
accept: Ya hay mucho tráfico para ser apenas las ocho.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it as a compliment to a friend: the cake came out good, and it was your first time.
yourTurn.answer: La torta quedó muy buena para ser la primera vez.
accept: La torta te quedó muy buena para ser la primera vez.
La torta te quedó muy buena para ser tu primera vez.
La torta quedó buena para ser la primera vez.
yourTurn.why: *Para ser la primera vez* is the standard "for a first time".

pitfalls.wrong: Por ser tan joven, sabe mucho.
pitfalls.right: Para ser tan joven, sabe mucho.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Por* would mean "because she's so young", which makes no sense here; "for someone so young" takes *para*.

pitfalls.wrong: Habla muy bien para tener un año aquí.
pitfalls.right: Habla muy bien para llevar un año aquí.
pitfalls.why: For a length of time, Spanish says *llevar*: *llevar un año aquí*.

pitfalls.wrong: No está mal por la primera vez.
pitfalls.right: No está mal para ser la primera vez.

personal: Give yourself a compliment that comes with an excuse, using *para ser* or *para llevar*.
